facts.fact: The Togolese government has launched urban addressing modernisation starting with Greater Lome (DAGL), building databases of coded and named roads and address points, with signage plaques and certification of doors, per the republicoftogo.com report.

facts.fact: Republic of Togo reports French firm Edenmap was retained to reorganise addressing across the thirteen communes of Greater Lome, where about 500,000 addresses remain to be created and about 13,000 of 16,000 recorded roads are still unnamed, per Edenmap's president.

The Grand Lome autonomous district (DAGL) presented on 17 December 2025 the feasibility study of a modernised addressing project to give every street a code and every home an official number, covering 5,000 km of roads and 538,000 doors across 13 communes.
allAfrica reports that the Societe des postes du Togo, with UPU support, is working on digital addressing.
